lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Morning, Captain! Nobody sails from Anchorage without their papers.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Papers means a GitHub account, and either a Copilot plan or your own model provider.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: That's the New page, where new work starts. You can change your theme any time in Settings.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Hints are my job, Captain. Decisions are yours.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Ahoy, Captain! Up here! I'm Wingman, your parrot and first mate.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Every island out here teaches a chapter of the GitHub Copilot app for Beginners course, and each one has a Seal to earn.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: We're on Anchorage Cay, where you'll set up the app. Nell's by the harbourmaster's door, so start with her.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Your tasks are in the top left. If you get stuck, press Q, and I'll give you a hint.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Right, I'll ride on your shoulder. Hints are my job. Decisions are yours!

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Welcome back, Captain! Your next task's in the top left.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: If the sign doesn't name your fork, don't pull the yes lever yet.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: You'll get unlimited retries here, so try the idea that feels safest.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Eight questions, Captain. No answers from me in there, only nudges.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Quick one, Captain: those are GitHub Actions workflows. The Clock Tower’s Automations are something else, saved agent tasks, and you’ll learn those much later.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Mill's dry today, Captain. Come back once your fork has its practice items.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: You’re the captain with the new fork? Suri Okoye. I keep the mill.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Pim and Pol had you turn on workflows in your fork's Actions tab. My mill shows what that does.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Here the gate’s your Actions tab. Pull the lever, then turn the channels with E until the spring reaches my wheel.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Lever first, then turn the channels. Follow the water from the spring.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Hear that wheel sing? Your practice checks can run now. Fair winds.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: There. The practice checks can run on your fork now.

lines.speaker: Suri
lines.text: Later chapters use those checks, so that's time well spent. Fair winds, Captain.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Crane’s ready when you are, Captain.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Not yet, Captain. Our crane adds the course's practice items to your fork. Bo gets your session ready first, by the pier foot.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: I'm Pim, and that's Pol. Once your session's ready, we'll load your fork with practice issues and pull requests.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: The crane's all set, Captain. Come up whenever you're ready.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Turn the capstan, pull Dry-Run, and read the Repository line before anything else.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Preview first, always. Then --yes, but only on your own fork.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Nine pennants, five notices, seven hulls, three seals. Your fork's ready for practice!

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Remember: --dry-run first, check the Repository line, then --yes.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Captain! I'm Pim, that's Pol. We add the course's practice items to new forks.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: The course has a setup script. It adds labels, the coloured pennants, and issues, the bounty notices.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Practice branches too, the practice hulls. The bugs stay on those, never on main.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: And pull requests, sealed inspection requests: changes to review, a feedback comment, and a check that fails on purpose.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: They’re training scenarios, not problems with your setup.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: First, a job on GitHub.com. Open your fork's Actions tab. New forks switch workflows off.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Select, I understand my workflows, go ahead and enable them. Then GitHub can run the practice checks.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Then the script, in the app's Terminal. Our crane works the same way. Turn the capstan to aim her, pull Dry-Run to preview, and read the Repository line on her sign.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Only when it names your own fork do you pull --yes.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Setup complete. Your fork has everything the course needs, Captain.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: In the app, you run both commands in that same Terminal tab, from the repository root.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Your fork's got its practice issues and pull requests now. You'll work through them in later chapters.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Hear that pawl? The script stops before changing a repository owned by an organization.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: There’s an --allow-shared-repository flag for that, used with --yes. Only when you’re authorized and the Repository line is exactly the target you meant.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Not today, though. Aim for your own ship.

lines.speaker: Pol
lines.text: Refused! That’s another captain’s fork. The script won’t change a repository you don’t own.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: This is the GitHub Copilot app. It's where you'll give Copilot's agents their orders and check their work.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Next, download and install the GitHub Copilot app for your system.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: I've put that page in your Logbook, download link and all. Press J whenever you need it, and every page you find ends up there too.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Once it's installed, open it and select Sign in to GitHub. If your company's account lives on GHE.com, choose Sign in to GitHub Enterprise Cloud instead.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: On Copilot Business or Enterprise, your organization has to switch on the GitHub Copilot app policy first.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: You'll also need Git, Node.js, and GitHub CLI. The list's in my chest here, with where to get each one.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: At Connect your repositories, carry on without adding one. You’ll connect your fork shortly.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Then pick a theme and select Finish. Here, your theme's your sails. The palette stand's right beside me.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Papers in order. Off you go!

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Get your papers from Nell first, Captain. Then we’ll talk charts.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Every captain needs their own chart. Fork the course repository on GitHub, so your practice work lands in your own copy.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Once you’ve forked it, add it to the app. Where would you start?

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: That link takes you straight to the fork page. It’s in your Logbook now, and under your task, whenever you need it.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: That plus opens this menu. Pick Add GitHub repository, search for copilot-app-for-beginners, and select your fork. The app clones it and adds it to the sidebar.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Mind the search, though. The original course can show up right beside your fork.

lines.speaker: Ezra
lines.text: Next, your session. Bo's right beside me, at his gear rack.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Your project shows under Projects? Good. Select the + next to it to start a project session.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Now, the workspace selector below the prompt box. Don’t trust the checkmark, it just shows the default.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Next, your tools. Open View, then Toggle Review Panel, and pick the Terminal tab. No tab? Select + and then Terminal.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Commands run there. Start with the four version checks on my rack. Each should print a version number.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: If one says command not found, install just that tool, then run the checks again.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: One more thing. GitHub CLI has its own sign-in, separate from the app. Run gh auth status, and make sure it shows the account that owns your fork.

lines.speaker: Bo
lines.text: Deck's ready, and your gear checks out. Pim and Pol add the practice items next, at the crane at the end of the pier.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Juno, your first mate. Setup’s done, so let’s give the crew their first order.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: In the app, you’d send this to the agent from your project session:

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: “Give me an overview of the copilot-app-for-beginners course repository. Focus on the learning path and the samples/book-app-web folder.”

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: You’ve been running commands in Terminal all morning. This one’s different. It’s a request for the agent.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Two fittings on the rail, just behind me. The brass speaking tube goes up to the crew, and the iron hatch goes down to the engine room. Your call, Captain.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: It’s a request for the agent, not a command. Pick the fitting on the rail that carries it.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: The crew’s proud of you, Captain. Wherever you sail next, they’re listening.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: The crew knows the ship now. Nell's waiting by your bow with the Harbormaster's Trial.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Hear that? The crew’s answering.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: They’ve summed up the course, chapter by chapter, and flagged samples/book-app-web. That’s the web sample you’ll use in later exercises.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: In the app, your reply will be worded differently. Models vary, and that's fine.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Commands go to the Terminal. Requests go to the agent, through the prompt box. That's setup done, Captain. Nell's waiting by your bow with the Harbormaster's Trial.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: That went to the engine room, Captain. Terminal runs commands like git --version. Requests to the agent go in the prompt box.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: That went to the engine room, Captain. Terminal runs commands, not requests.

lines.speaker: Pim
lines.text: Your first mate’s waiting by your ship, Captain. Juno’s got your first order ready.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Fine colours, Captain. Next, your own copy of the course. Ezra's at his chart table, down by the pier.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Pick your sails at the palette stand, then select Finish.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: A sealed captain! Fair winds.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: No ship leaves Anchorage without a name, Captain, and yours has been waiting all morning.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Fair winds to her, and to all who sail in her!

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: She suits you, Captain. Fair winds.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: Setup's done, Captain. Before your ship gets her name, there's the Harbormaster's Trial: eight questions on what you've set up.

lines.speaker: Nell
lines.text: The Seal of Anchorage, and well earned. Now, about that ship.

lines.speaker: Juno
lines.text: Crew’s aboard, Captain.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Right, a quick sailing lesson. The gangway’s down now, so walk up it to take the helm. W and S trim the sails, and A and D steer.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: The compass up top points back to the pier. Bring her alongside and press E, and I’ll help you dock.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Port Meridian’s east on the chart, but she’s not ready for visitors yet. Until she is, these waters are yours.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Every island has a song, Captain. Come back once your crew’s heard your first words, and I’ll play you this one.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Ah, the new captain. Sit a moment. The course you’re sailing has a song running through it: a recording studio.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Before you record anything, you get the studio ready. You sign in, plug in your gear, load the song, and run a quick soundcheck.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: You’ve just done the sailor’s version: papers signed, the chart forked, your own deck, and a first word to your crew.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Next comes Port Meridian, where you’ll learn why the app matters and tour its rooms. I’ll travel on ahead.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Fair winds, Captain. Meridian’s plaza has the best acoustics in the isles.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Port Meridian! This island’s Chapter 01, a tour of the Copilot app itself.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Tobias trades in the plaza, up the stair street. Start with him, and follow the compass.

lines.speaker: Wingman
lines.text: Port Meridian’s north-east, Captain. Follow the compass, and dock by the east arm.

lines.speaker: Tobias
lines.text: Ah, a captain from Anchorage! You’ve got the app set up. So why use it at all?

lines.speaker: Tobias
lines.text: Copilot in your editor or terminal is grand, right next to the code you’ve got open.

lines.speaker: Tobias
lines.text: The hard part is supervising agent work from start to finish. Plans, edits, tests, previews, pull requests.

lines.speaker: Tobias
lines.text: See my table? Four headaches every captain knows. Match each one to what the app adds.

lines.speaker: Tobias
lines.text: Mind you, the app isn’t a replacement for your editor. Keep that for deep coding.

lines.speaker: Tobias
lines.text: When you want the full editor, the app opens the project in VS Code for you.

lines.speaker: Tobias
lines.text: I’ve put a note about your editor in your Logbook too.

lines.speaker: Tobias
lines.text: Now, Mina knows every corner of this town, and of the app. She’s by the fountain.

lines.speaker: Tobias
lines.text: Keep your editor close and the app closer, Captain.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Have a word with Tobias first. He’s at his table, just there.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Welcome to Meridian! This town’s laid out just like the app’s sidebar. Come and see.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: The Voyage Office is New, the landing view. Every new chat or project session starts there.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: The Bounty Board is My work, your GitHub inbox. Issues, pull requests and review requests.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: The practice items from your setup script are pinned up there, ready to work on.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: The Clock Tower is Automations. Agent tasks that run on demand, on a schedule, or when something happens on GitHub.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: And the Outfitter is Customize, for skills, MCP servers and plugins. You won’t need those until later chapters.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Below those, the sidebar keeps your Projects, with your chats and your project sessions.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: I’ve filed all four in your Logbook. Press J any time.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: Lyra’s playing at the tavern, just west of here. She’ll show you how a chat works.

lines.speaker: Mina
lines.text: New, My work, Automations, Customize. You know your way around now!

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: I’m still tuning up, Captain. Come back once Mina’s shown you round.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Captain! I told you this plaza had the best acoustics.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: A producer doesn’t run every take the same way. Some need close direction. Some need the arrangement charted first.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: And some quick questions just need a fast answer. That’s a chat.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: To start one, hover over Chats in the sidebar, and select the plus that appears.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: There. The picker says Chat, so there’s no branch, no worktree, and no files change.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Try the prompt on that page in the app. It asks when to use a chat and when to use a project session.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Project sessions are Anders’s trade. He’s at the shipyard, at the west end of the quay.

lines.speaker: Lyra
lines.text: Quick question? Start a chat. That’s the whole song.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Hear Lyra out at the tavern first. Then come and see the shipyard.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Chats are for questions. When the agent needs your repository, you want a project session.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Changing code, running tests, making a pull request. That’s project work.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Each project session gets its own new worktree by default, like a hull on its own slipway.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Your Chapter 00 setup session was the exception. You picked Local repository for that one.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Go back to that session and send the prompt on this page. It tours the book app sample, file by file.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Now, my crates are all muddled. Chat work goes on the tavern plates, project work on the slipway plates.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Push each crate onto its plate, Captain. The lever by the gate starts the yard over.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Every crate in its place. You can tell a question from a job.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Rhea’s by your ship on the east arm. She’ll take you sailing.

lines.speaker: Anders
lines.text: Questions to a chat, jobs to a project session. Good work.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Anders first, Captain. Then we’ll sail.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Captain! Welcome to the Academy. Today’s lesson is session modes.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: The mode sets how independently the agent works. Interactive, Plan, and Autopilot.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: They aren’t levels to unlock. You pick the one that suits the task. Let’s sail all three.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Board your ship. Each buoy out in the bay is a helm to sail.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: The three helms are out in the bay, Captain. Board your ship and sail them.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: You’ve sailed all three. Now, which mode suits which task?

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Oren’s up at the observatory. Take the lift at the top of the arm.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Match the mode to the job, Captain. Every time.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: The stars will keep, Captain. Sail with Rhea first.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Ah, you came up. The mode sets how independently the agent works. The model decides how it thinks.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: The model control sits below the prompt box, right beside the mode selector.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Open it to find Model and Effort. If it says Auto, the app picks a model for your task.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Careful, though. Auto isn’t Autopilot. Autopilot is a mode. Auto is about the model.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: For a quick explanation, keep the defaults. For a hard bug across several files, try a stronger model and higher effort.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Higher effort can help. It doesn’t guarantee the right answer.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Try it with the prompt on this page. The answer should point to App.tsx in the book app.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: And you can change the model or effort mid-session, without changing the mode.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Pell keeps the Hall of Records, across the courtyard. Ask about settings.

lines.speaker: Oren
lines.text: Defaults for the simple things, Captain. More effort for the hard ones.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Records are kept in order, Captain. See Oren first.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Settings! Nine areas, and I keep a record of every one.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: General has updates, storage and the theme. Accounts lets you add another GitHub account.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Sessions is where you manage sessions and chats, the response style, and app-wide instructions.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Model providers connects other providers with your own API keys. It doesn’t replace the model picker.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: And Voice dictation turns speech into prompt text, if you’d like to try it. That part’s optional.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: I’ve filed the voice dictation steps in your Logbook as well.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: The Admiral’s waiting on her terrace. She’ll want to hear what you’ve learned.

lines.speaker: Pell
lines.text: Can’t find a setting? Look for the closest area. Versions vary.

lines.speaker: Admiral
lines.text: You’ll have your exam, Captain, once you’ve been round the town.

lines.speaker: Admiral
lines.text: Captain. You’ve toured the whole app in one afternoon.

lines.speaker: Admiral
lines.text: Answer my questions, and the Seal of Meridian is yours.

lines.speaker: Admiral
lines.text: Take your time, Captain. The exam’s here whenever you’re ready.

lines.speaker: Admiral
lines.text: Well sailed! The Seal of Meridian. Now watch the lighthouse.

lines.speaker: Admiral
lines.text: Chapter 02 is sessions, worktrees and context. That island’s still being charted, but the course is ready when you are.

lines.speaker: Admiral
lines.text: Fair winds, Captain. Meridian’s proud of you.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Interactive helm. We’ll sail one leg at a time, and I’ll check with you at every mark.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Mark reached. Shall we sail the next leg?

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: That’s Interactive. You were involved at every step.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Next, the Plan buoy. Look for the orange flag.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Plan helm. Here’s the route I’ve charted. Look it over, then approve it.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Plan approved. Now she sails it straight through.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: That’s Plan. You saw the whole route before anything moved.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Last one, the Autopilot buoy with the green flag.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Autopilot helm. Give her the destination, your berth, and she’ll take it from here.

lines.speaker: Rhea
lines.text: Home, and not a single stop. That’s Autopilot, for a task that’s clearly defined.
